source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The accepted test imports Alice's public key with the helper's default verified acceptance, reads alice-signed.eml, and extracts the armored signed body. It then creates a SyntheticMessage with an explicit sender, subject and fixed date rather than handing the raw MIME file to addMessages. The fake-server API expects SyntheticMessage objects and uses their message IDs. Keep the fixture body, fixed date and accepted key together when changing this positive case. The final test expectation is the verified icon state; no message or cryptographic verification ran during this source study. The current exchange path and MockServer inheritance are later accepted structure, separate from the owned ews-path change.
title: The EWS signed-message test builds a dated synthetic message from the fixture body
